title: Minimum-wage effective dates and restaurant/retail realized volatility
claim: A public minimum-wage effective-date calendar does not robustly predict higher realized volatility or downside variance in restaurant and retail equity baskets relative to SPY, XLY, or low-labor-tech controls.

evidence.sample: yfinance adjusted close from 2020-01-02 to 2026-07-02; 20 usable public effective-date clusters from 2021-01-01 to 2026-01-01 after excluding incomplete post-window events.

lookahead_controls: Event dates are known before trading and are mapped to the next trading day.
Outcomes are post-event realized variance/downside windows relative to pre-event windows; no same-day signal-return strategy is used.
The incomplete 2026-07-01 post-event window is excluded automatically.
limitations: This is a public event-date proxy, not a state-border discontinuity design.
Public companies have diversified store footprints and no store-level state exposure is measured.
Minimum-wage changes may be priced before implementation at legislative, ballot, or earnings-call dates.
Jan-1 events are seasonal; DID controls and placebo tests reduce but do not eliminate confounding.
next_steps: Only reopen if store-level state exposure or county-border public-company mapping is available.
If reopened, move event timing from implementation dates to passage/announcement dates and earnings-call discussion dates.
